Open-source gradient library from Pittsburgh hits 1,800 stars

By Jordan Lee · Sept. 12, 2026

When Alex Rivera released fastgrad two years ago, it was a weekend project for compressing gradients in data-parallel training. This month the library passed 1,800 stars on GitHub and is now used by three university research labs.

"We cut our training bill by a third," said a researcher at one of the labs, who asked not to be named because the results are unpublished. The labs run fastgrad on clusters of up to 512 GPUs.

Rivera, a machine-learning engineer at Fernhill Robotics, says the next release adds support for mixed-precision training. The project's maintainers have merged contributions from more than forty developers.

Alex Rivera will present the work at the Pittsburgh ML Systems meetup in November.
